Implementation Plan

Plan for the CI failure triage on PR #7101 (issue: check-failure-triage generation 1)

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends Regression tests wired by the CI wiring guard (part 2)
Scope-mode justification: The CI failure comes from one unwired file, and the fix is to wire it. `tests/test_clarify_sandbox_base_image_preseed.py` is on the planning ref (`main`, `7a620daff53ddbb43e009963d0ad198f56f58039`), but no `.github/workflows/*.yml` names it. `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py::test_every_test_file_runs_in_a_workflow` therefore fails in `static-checks`, and the `lint` aggregate fails after it. Adding one path to an existing pytest step is the complete fix. Under the Boil the Lake rule (§6 Core Priorities: Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), the extra cost here is fixing one sentence in the pending changelog fragment that says the test is not yet run by CI. That is one line, so this plan includes it so the docs don't contradict the code. Nothing else is in scope: no new job, no change to the guard, no allowlist entry.

Automation / scheduler surface (§20.E)
- New script: none. Extended script: none. This only changes existing files.
- Entry point: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which already runs on `pull_request` and `push`. The test runs in the existing step "Regression tests wired by the CI wiring guard (part 2)" of the `tests-promote-stall-and-review` job.
- New long-running supervisor: none.
- DB work: none.
- `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry: none needed, because no script or supervisor is added.

Planning ref context
- `git rev-parse HEAD`: `7a620daff53ddbb43e009963d0ad198f56f58039`. Resolved checkout ref: `main`. Integration branch metadata: none. Integration branch mismatch: `unknown`, which is not `true`, so this is not blocked.
- Conflict note: the triage issue says the test was "absent from the provided `/source` snapshot". On the planning ref it is present: 455 lines, 13 `test_*` functions, and an `if __name__ == "__main__"` entry. PR #7101 (`ai/issue-7099`) has since landed it on `main` together with `changelog.d/6985-clarify-sandbox-base-image-mirror.md`. That fragment itself says "The regression test `tests/test_clarify_sandbox_base_image_preseed.py` is not yet run by any `ci.yml` step." So the failure now also reproduces on `main`, not only on the PR head. A grep of `.github/workflows/*.yml` and `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py` finds no reference to the file, and it is not in `UNWIRED_ALLOWLIST`.
- Conflict note 2: the triage suggests the "Prebuilt sandbox image tests" step (now `ci.yml` ~line 640). That step is in `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`, and the `ci.yml` comment at ~line 1315 says that job "measured 19.6 of its 20 minutes on main (2026-10-09) and timed out on PR heads". This plan therefore does not put the test there (see D1).

1. Files likely to change
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: in job `tests-promote-stall-and-review`, step `Regression tests wired by the CI wiring guard (part 2)` (~line 1253), add one continuation line `            tests/test_clarify_sandbox_base_image_preseed.py \`. Keep the list alphabetical: it goes between `tests/test_changelog_fragment_contract.py \` and `tests/test_codex_heartbeat.py \`. Use 2-space YAML indentation (§11) and the same 12-space continuation indent as the neighbouring lines. The step name, `run:` header, `set -euo pipefail` and the pytest flags (`-q -p no:cacheprovider`) stay as they are.
- `changelog.d/6985-clarify-sandbox-base-image-mirror.md`: this is a correction of existing text, which §25 and CLAUDE.md §20 allow for an unfolded fragment. In the last paragraph of "### For contributors", replace "The regression test `tests/test_clarify_sandbox_base_image_preseed.py` is not yet run by any `ci.yml` step." with "The regression test `tests/test_clarify_sandbox_base_image_preseed.py` runs in the `ci.yml` step \"Regression tests wired by the CI wiring guard (part 2)\"." If a release has already folded and deleted the fragment, skip this edit. Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md` directly.
- No other files. Do not add an `UNWIRED_ALLOWLIST` entry: the test runs on a stock runner with PyYAML, bash and a fake `docker`, so it can run in CI. Do not change `tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py`.

2. Functions or modules to implement
- None. This is a workflow wiring change only.

3. Data structures affected
- None.

4. API or interface changes
- None. No step `name:`, `id:`, job id, env var or log prefix is renamed (§10). The `CI / lint` aggregate and its `needs` list are unchanged.

## Decisions

### D1 — Which CI step runs the new test
- Chosen: add it to the existing pytest list in "Regression tests wired by the CI wiring guard (part 2)" (`tests-promote-stall-and-review`).
- Alternatives considered: (a) the "Prebuilt sandbox image tests" step in `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`, as the triage issue suggested; (b) a new dedicated step; (c) the "Clarify loop guard unit tests" step, which runs files as `python3 <file>` scripts; (d) an `UNWIRED_ALLOWLIST` entry.
- Why: agents.md (CI job layout) says a new test file goes into an existing step, and the part-2 step was created for exactly this kind of guard-wired regression test. (a) would add time to the job that is documented at 19.6/20 minutes and has timed out on PR heads. (b) adds structure that isn't needed. (c) would work through the file's `__main__` entry, but that step is not a pytest list, so a pytest-native module fits better in part 2. (d) is forbidden because the test can run in CI (the triage itself says "Do not allowlist or disable a runnable test").

### D2 — Whether to fix the stale changelog sentence
- Chosen: fix it in the same PR, as long as the fragment has not been folded yet.
- Alternatives considered: leave it alone; add a new fragment.
- Why: once this lands the sentence is false, and the fragment will be folded into `CHANGELOG.md` at release, which then can't be edited directly. A one-line correction is cheaper than a new fragment and avoids shipping contradictory docs. A contributor-only CI wiring change doesn't need a fragment of its own.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries: none are changed. The new line only adds a test path to an existing `run:` body with no `${{ }}` expressions, so there is no new place for untrusted input to be interpolated into the workflow (Integration-ref trust boundary rule).
- Authorization: no new endpoint, permission, secret or token. The `ci.yml` job permissions stay as they are.
- External input: the test drives the real "Pre-seed clarify sandbox base image" `run:` body against a fake `docker` in a temp directory. It needs no network or credentials, and the step it tests runs `docker` through `env -u OPENROUTER_API_KEY -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Abuse cases: someone could later drop this line to hide a regression in the clarify pre-seed step. The wiring guard is the backstop against that, and this change brings the guard back to green. No money-handling surface is involved.

5. Risks and edge cases
- Automation-path guard: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is under `.github/`, so implement needs an automation-path grant (`IMPLEMENT_AUTOMATION_PATH_GUARD`). This issue has no `files_touched` block. If it was authored by the `GH_PAT` login (the triage poster), it gets `reason=pipeline_author_no_allowlist`, an open grant. If it was authored by a different account (for example the fine-grained `CHECK_TRIAGE_ISSUES_TOKEN` owner, if that differs from the `GH_PAT` login), implement will stop with `ai:scope-blocked`. Recovery then goes through the unblock judge's regrant path or an operator, not through this plan.
- If `main` has already been fixed by a concurrent PR (the path is already in some workflow), the edit must not add a second reference. The implementer should check first with `grep -rn test_clarify_sandbox_base_image_preseed .github/workflows/` and finish as a no-op if it's already wired. A duplicate in another job would trip `test_no_step_runs_in_more_than_one_job` only if whole steps were duplicated, but a duplicate is still wasted CI time.
- Job budget: the test spawns short bash subprocesses against a fake `docker` (13 cases) and should take seconds. `tests-promote-stall-and-review` has a 20-minute budget, and #4707 measured it at about 8.2 minutes, so there is plenty of headroom.
- Test health is unverified: `main` has never run this module in CI, so it might fail once it is wired. If it fails, fix the actual defect (in the test or in `clarify.yml`'s pre-seed step). Do not skip or allowlist it (§15, root-cause rule).
- Workflow size: `ci.yml` is 99,534 bytes, far below the 480,000-byte §24 guard.
- `static-checks` also runs YAML lint and actionlint, so the continuation line must keep the trailing ` \` and the exact indentation.

6. Testing considerations
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py`: must pass. Today it fails with exactly this file listed.
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_clarify_sandbox_base_image_preseed.py`: the newly wired module must pass.
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_ci_job_split_contract.py`: confirms there is no cross-job step duplication and the budgets are unchanged.
- `yamllint` / `actionlint` on `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, as in `static-checks`.
- If the fragment is edited: `tests/test_changelog_fragment_contract.py`.
- Note: pytest and PyYAML are not installed in this planning sandbox, so none of these were run here. They are all UNVERIFIED locally, and the PR's CI run is the authority on the pinned toolchain.

7. Pre-execution self-check
- The plan fixes the cited root cause: the guard's assertion names exactly one unwired file, and this plan wires it.
- It edits no protected-by-hand files (`.claude/**`, `agents.md`) and adds n
